observed.facings.png: Four facings at one scale. South is only two small dark iron hook caps. East and west are short, wide wooden ladder sections: two thick horizontal log stringers with iron bands, joined by vertical round rungs, with iron hooks at the wall end. North is a tall ladder seen face-on: two round timber stringers and horizontal rungs between two iron-banded wooden guide rails, with curled iron hooks on top. The rails narrow toward the bottom.
observed.south.png: Two small black-iron U-shaped hooks side by side near the lower middle. No timber shows. They read as the curled rail tops at the near rim.
observed.east.png: A ladder section in the right part of the canvas. Two thick, slightly sloped horizontal wooden stringers with iron straps; four or five vertical round rungs between them; dark iron hooks on the right ends, top and bottom. The stringers spread apart toward the right and converge toward the left. It has warm brown wood grain and a dark outline.
observed.north.png: A face-on wooden ladder in the upper middle. Round timber stringers with end caps, about eight horizontal rungs whose gaps shrink lower down, two outer iron-banded wooden guide rails, and black curled hooks at the top. The whole thing tapers slightly toward the bottom.
observed.west.png: A mirror of east, in the left part of the canvas: hooks on the left ends and stringers converging toward the right.
observed.scale.png: The lowered ladders composed in a pit panel with a vanilla human. The north ladder hangs from the north rim down the light wall band to the dark pit-floor edge. The east and west ladders sit on their side wall bands with hooks at the rim, not reaching the dark floor. South shows only the two hooks on the near rim. Size is plausible against the human.
observed.wall_context.png: Lowered (left) and raised (right) pits. Raised north: the ladder is slid up, with its top above the north rim on the ground, and the guide rails still run from the rim hooks down the wall band. Raised east/west: the ladder section is pushed outward past the side rim onto the ground, and thin rails still run from the rim back across the band. Raised south: a short ladder top rises above the near rim between the two hooks.
observed.variants_1.png: Raised north alone: the ladder is shifted up so its top stands above the hooks. The guide rails, with iron clamps, run below it down to where the band ends. Nothing floats; the clamps hold it.
observed.variants_2.png: Raised east alone: the ladder block is shifted right past the hook line. Thinner horizontal guide rails with iron end caps extend left from the hooks, under and behind the ladder.
observed.variants_3.png: Raised west: a mirror of raised east.
observed.variants_4.png: Raised south: a short wooden ladder top with two round posts and four rungs stands above two iron hooks at the bottom.
observed.variants_5.png: Zoom sheet. North lowered: the rails converge with depth, the rungs are round timber, and the iron bands are visible. East/west lowered: steep, sitting on the light wall band between the rim line and the dark floor, with the stringers' long axis horizontal (east-west). Raised states: the ladder pushed past the rim, with rails left on the band. Wood grain is clear at zoom, and the stringers and rungs read as solid poles.

CAMERA.seen: The north wall face recedes downward with converging rails. The side views are the north view turned a quarter and squeezed into the wall band, as the card describes. There are no circular faces to the camera.

BORE.seen: There are no pipes or hoses. The hook tops are curled solid iron and show no open bore.

PORTS.seen: The card lists no code ports, and there is no coupler, hose or cord. The wall_context composites stand in for the assembled view.

WALL_LEAN.seen: In wall_context the east ladder has its hooks at the east rim and converges toward the pit (screen-left); the west ladder mirrors it. Both match the north view converging with depth.

WALL_AXIS.seen: North: the long axis runs screen-up/down the face. East/west: the stringers run east-west, from the rim hooks inward across the band, not along the wall.

PORTS_DRAWN.seen: No code ports, and no drawn connectors. The hooks are rail tops, not ports.

LAYERS.seen: In the wall_context raised states, the ladder draws over its guide rails and the hooks sit at the rim. Nothing obviously draws out of order.

ROTATIONS.seen: The same wood palette, iron straps, hooks and rail-plus-ladder construction appear on every facing and in both states.

SIGNATURE.seen: A wooden ladder on two guide rails with hooks curling over the rim, lowered and raised (slid up past the rim, still held by the rails).

MATERIAL.seen: Warm brown wood grain on round poles with iron straps and dark iron hooks. It reads as timber and iron.

FOOTPRINT.seen: Lowered: the ladders sit within their wall bands. Raised: the top extends past the rim in the up-the-wall direction, as intended. South is tiny by design. The 479% height spread is real (south is only what stands above the near rim), not an error.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-outs on transparent canvases, with no ground patch or shadow.

OURS.seen: Script-painted own art matching the v4/v5 provenance. No vanilla or mod donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Fire-escape spacing, not dense. The lowered north view is preserved. E/W are steep and stay off the dark pit floor. Raised is no longer broken: the rails still hold the ladder. The side stringers are thick logs, not skeletal. The timber is visibly heavier (1.4x) than slim tubes.

LEGIBLE.seen: At normal zoom in scale.png and wall_context, all four facings read as ladders. The north rungs are thin but the pattern of rungs reads.

reply.image_seen: 1: four lowered facings; 2: two exposed south hooks; 3: compressed wooden east ladder; 4: tapered north ladder with open rung gaps; 5: mirrored west ladder; 6: lowered ladders around a pit beside a human; 7: lowered and raised wall compositions; 8: raised north ladder overlapping its guides. Separate raised east/west closeups, the zoom sheet and an explicitly identified in-game assembled capture are absent.

concerns.evidence: In image 4, the rungs have visible rounded thickness, ochre highlights and darker wooden undersides; the stringers and outer guides are substantial timber members. Image 6 preserves an open ladder silhouette. Rungs being narrower than stringers does not establish that the requested wood heft is missing, and small projected rung thickness alone is advisory.

The cited variants_2.png and variants_3.png are absent. Image 7 shows narrow exposed guide sections behind the raised side ladders, but their small presentation and overlap do not reliably establish whether their timber thickness disagrees with the north guides. Full-size raised east/west images would settle this.

The visible components are solid timber rungs, stringers and guides with curled mounting hooks. No open pipe or hose bore is depicted. The bore-plane check can be answered ok from the supplied textures.
The card defines zero ports. The visible dark curls terminate the guide rails as mounting hooks; no hose, cord, coupler or fluid connector is drawn. The port check can therefore be answered ok.
